glossaryReview.reasoning: A sound convention. Deut 1:6-4:40 is a single Mosaic discourse, and leaving out the outer marks avoids nesting three levels deep. Checked in the chapter: vv 1-40 unmarked, 4:6 and 4:10 in double marks, 4:41 narration. Embedded speech in Ex 33:5, 12 and Num 18:24, 26, 29-32 is nested correctly. The founder should confirm it before Deut 1-3 and 5 are translated (F8).

Each listed site re-checked in the source. The source carries one Ketiv/Qere (Num 21:32) and one extraordinary point (Num 21:30, U+05C4 over the rēš of ʾăšer). The Deut 4:30 athnach is on hāʾēlleh, and Deut 4:37 has singular suffixes. Every MT reading is construable and the versions are recorded. The only error, the Ketiv vocalization at Num 21:32, is in that verse's commentary, not in this entry.

The clauses are sound and match the exodus-woh and Kings practice (checked: exodus-woh 20:3, 20 'elohim'; 1 Kgs 8:23 'no elohim like you'). One factual fix: the rationale argues that at Deut 4:7 the plural adjective qərōḇîm makes ʾĕlōhîm a class. Plural attributives also stand with ʾĕlōhîm of YHWH himself (Deut 5:26 ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm; Josh 24:19 ʾĕlōhîm qədōšîm; 1 Sam 17:26), so the adjective proves nothing. The comparison 'as YHWH our Elohim' carries the decision. Restate the argument on that basis, in all three overlays and in the DEU-WOH-4:7 commentary. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-proper-names: Option (a) for this wave: keep the split, do not retro-edit signed-off chapters, and record it in the corpus. Prefer the transliterated 'Moshe'/'Par'oh', because they are the only English forms left in an otherwise transliterated Torah and the ASV equivalence table already serves readers of the canon's KJV-based English. Prefer the tz spelling 'Mitzrayim', since tz is already the Torah rule for every other tsade. Keep 'the Egyptians' for the population (amend the central gentilic 'Mitsri', which no volume uses), and bring isaiah-woh 'Egypt' into the same decision.

Ex 13:9 'the law of YHWH' is a Deuteronomic-style formula (ASV, NRSV 'law'), and Ex 16:4 'my law' (ASV, NRSV) or 'my instruction' (NJPS 'teaching') is a founder preference. Keep Isaiah's 'teaching' as the prophetic clause of the same central entry.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-merism: Confirm 'the heavens and the earth' for the merism outside Gen 1 (exodus-woh 20:11; Deut 4:26, 39). State explicitly that the creation formulas of Isaiah ('created the skies', 'spread out the earth') render the physical sky 'skies', so that the two practices read as one rule.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F9-kapporet: Keep 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV). It preserves the link with kippēr and Lev 16 that 'cover' loses, and the dispute is fully recorded in the commentary.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֜לֶּה מַסְעֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצְא֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

i18n.en: These are the journeys of the children of Yisra'el, when they went out from the land of Mitsrayim by their hosts under the hand of Moses and Aharon.

notes.official: *ʾēlleh masʿê ḇənê-yiśrāʾēl* 'These are the journeys of the children of Yisra'el': the chapter lists forty-two stations from Ra'meses to the plains of Moab, a number sometimes related to the forty years (Davies 1979; Levine 2000). *ləṣiḇʾōṯām* 'by their hosts', the tribal divisions of 1:3. Names follow `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`, whose table gives the ASV form of every station; stations already named in exodus-woh (Sukkot, Etam, Pi-haChirot, Baal-Tzefon, Migdol, Elim, Sin, Refidim, Sinai) keep their published forms. *mēʾereṣ miṣrayim* 'from the land of Mitsrayim' (central `mitsrayim`; `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־מוֹצָאֵיהֶ֛ם לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה מַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם לְמוֹצָאֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Moses wrote down their goings out according to their journeys, by the mouth of YHWH; and these are their journeys according to their goings out.

notes.official: *wayyiḵtōḇ mōšeh ʾeṯ-môṣāʾêhem ləmasʿêhem ... wəʾēlleh masʿêhem ləmôṣāʾêhem* 'And Moses wrote down their goings out according to their journeys ... and these are their journeys according to their goings out': the line keeps the ASV wording, which preserves the chiasm of the Hebrew. *ʿal-pî YHWH* 'by the mouth of YHWH', literal as exodus-woh 17:1 (ASV 'by the commandment'); it may qualify either the writing or the journeys.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מֵֽרַעְמְסֵס֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן מִֽמָּחֳרַ֣ת הַפֶּ֗סַח יָצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Ra'meses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow of the Passover the children of Yisra'el went out with a high hand before the eyes of all the Egyptians,

notes.official: *wayyisʿû mēraʿməsēs* 'And they journeyed from Ra'meses' (central `raamses-eastern-delta-store-city-toponym`; ASV Rameses). *mimmāḥŏraṯ happesaḥ* 'on the morrow of the Passover', the fifteenth of the first month (Ex 12:6, 29-34; Lev 23:5-6). *bəyāḏ rāmâ* 'with a high hand', openly and defiantly (Ex 14:8). *ləʿênê kol-miṣrāyim* 'before the eyes of all the Egyptians' (draft 'all Mitsrayim'; ASV 'all the Egyptians'): here and in v 4 *miṣrayim* is the population, and the line follows exodus-woh's practice of 'the Egyptians' for the people (Ex 3:9; 14 passim), recorded in `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah` as a departure from the gentilic 'Mitsri' of the central `mitsrayim`.

paragraphs.text: וּמִצְרַ֣יִם מְקַבְּרִ֗ים אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּהֶ֖ם כָּל־בְּכ֑וֹר וּבֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁפָטִֽים׃

i18n.en: while the Egyptians were burying those whom YHWH had struck among them, all the firstborn; and upon their elohim YHWH had executed judgments.

notes.official: *ûmiṣrayim məqabbərîm* 'while the Egyptians were burying' (draft 'Mitsrayim was burying'): a plural participle with *miṣrayim* as subject, hence 'the Egyptians' (see v 3). *ûḇēʾlōhêhem ʿāśâ YHWH šəp̄āṭîm* 'and upon their elohim YHWH had executed judgments', as announced at Ex 12:12; lower-case 'elohim' for the deities of Mitsrayim (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 3; central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֑ס וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּסֻכֹּֽת׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el journeyed from Ra'meses and camped in Sukkot.

notes.official: Sukkot (ASV Succoth; central `sukkot-toponym-and-festival-etymology`), as Ex 12:37; Ra'meses (central `raamses-eastern-delta-store-city-toponym`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Sukkot and camped in Etam, which is at the edge of the wilderness.

notes.official: Etam (ASV Etham), 'at the edge of the wilderness', as Ex 13:20 (central `sukkot-toponym-and-festival-etymology`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵתָ֔ם וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵ֖י בַּ֣עַל צְפ֑וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מִגְדֹּֽל׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Etam and turned back to Pi-haChirot, which is before Baal-Tzefon; and they camped before Migdol.

notes.official: *wayyāšoḇ ʿal-pî haḥîrōṯ* 'and turned back to Pi-haChirot (ASV Pi-hahiroth), which is before Baal-Tzefon (ASV Baal-zephon)', as exodus-woh 14:2, 9; Migdol as there.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַֽחִירֹ֔ת וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַיָּ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּ֑רָה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר אֵתָ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from before haChirot and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness; and they went a three days' journey in the wilderness of Etam and camped in Marah.

notes.official: *mippənê haḥîrōṯ* 'from before haChirot': the MT lacks the *pî* of v 7, and the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Peshitta and the Vulgate read 'from Pi-haChirot'; the line translates the MT, as the ASV does ('from before Hahiroth') (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *wayyaʿaḇrû ḇəṯôḵ-hayyām* 'and passed through the midst of the sea', the crossing of Ex 14. Marah, 'bitter' (Ex 15:23), keeps its familiar form.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֵילִ֑מָה וּ֠בְאֵילִם שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֞ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֛יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים תְּמָרִ֖ים וַיַּחֲנוּ־שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Marah and came to Elim; and in Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm-trees; and they camped there.

notes.official: Elim, with its twelve springs and seventy palm-trees (Ex 15:27). *šiḇʿîm təmārîm* 'seventy palm-trees' (ASV 'threescore and ten'): the central glossary keeps the archaic count only for the seventy souls of Gen 46.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֵילִ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Elim and camped by the Sea of Reeds.

notes.official: *wayyaḥănû ʿal-yam-sûp̄* 'and camped by the Sea of Reeds' (central `yam-suf-sea-of-reeds-vs-red-sea-geographical-textual-cross-corpus`): a station not mentioned in Exodus, between Elim and the wilderness of Sin, where the name is usually taken to refer to the Gulf of Suez (Davies 1979).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִיַּם־ס֑וּף וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִדְבַּר־סִֽין׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from the Sea of Reeds and camped in the wilderness of Sin.

notes.official: The wilderness of Sin (Ex 16:1), between Elim and Sinai (central `yam-suf-sea-of-reeds-vs-red-sea-geographical-textual-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֑ין וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּדָפְקָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sin and camped in Dofqah.

notes.official: Dofqah (ASV Dophkah) and Alush (v 13) do not occur in Exodus; Dofqah has been linked, speculatively, with the Egyptian turquoise mines of Serabit el-Khadim (Egyptian *mfkꜣt* 'turquoise').

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִדָּפְקָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאָלֽוּשׁ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Dofqah and camped in Alush.

notes.official: Alush (ASV Alush), like Dofqah (v 12) absent from the Exodus itinerary.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאָל֑וּשׁ וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ם וְלֹא־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֥ם מַ֛יִם לָעָ֖ם לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Alush and camped in Refidim, and there was no water there for the people to drink.

notes.official: Refidim (ASV Rephidim; exodus-woh 17:1), with the note that there was no water (Ex 17:1-7).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרְפִידִ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Refidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

notes.official: The wilderness of Sinai (Ex 19:1-2): the list passes over the year at Sinai in one line.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּקִבְרֹ֥ת הַֽתַּאֲוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sinai and camped in Qivrot-haTa'avah.

notes.official: Qivrot-haTa'avah (ASV Kibroth-hattaavah), 'graves of craving', named at 11:34; the etymology is given in that chapter, not here, and the name is not glossed.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקִּבְרֹ֣ת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Qivrot-haTa'avah and camped in Chatzerot.

notes.official: Chatzerot (ASV Hazeroth), 11:35; 12:16.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵחֲצֵרֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִתְמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Chatzerot and camped in Ritmah.

notes.official: Ritmah (ASV Rithmah), from *rōṯem* 'broom bush' (the plant of 1 Kgs 19:4). The stations of vv 18-29 occur only in this list, and their locations are unknown.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרִתְמָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִמֹּ֥ן פָּֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Ritmah and camped in Rimmon-Peretz.

notes.official: Rimmon-Peretz (ASV Rimmon-perez).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרִמֹּ֣ן פָּ֑רֶץ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּלִבְנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Rimmon-Peretz and camped in Livnah.

notes.official: Livnah (ASV Libnah), not the Shephelah city of Josh 10:29.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִלִּבְנָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִסָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Livnah and camped in Rissah.

notes.official: Rissah (ASV Rissah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרִסָּ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בִּקְהֵלָֽתָה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Rissah and camped in Qehelatah.

notes.official: Qehelatah (ASV Kehelathah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקְּהֵלָ֑תָה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּהַר־שָֽׁפֶר׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Qehelatah and camped at Mount Shefer.

notes.official: *har-šep̄er* 'Mount Shefer' (ASV Shepher).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵֽהַר־שָׁ֑פֶר וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּחֲרָדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Mount Shefer and camped in Charadah.

notes.official: Charadah (ASV Haradah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵחֲרָדָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמַקְהֵלֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Charadah and camped in Maqhelot.

notes.official: Maqhelot (ASV Makheloth).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמַּקְהֵלֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּתָֽחַת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Maqhelot and camped in Tachat.

notes.official: Tachat (ASV Tahath).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִתָּ֑חַת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּתָֽרַח׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Tachat and camped in Terach.

notes.official: Terach (ASV Terah); genesis-woh prints both 'Terach' and 'Terah' for the name of Avraham's father.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִתָּ֑רַח וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִתְקָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Terach and camped in Mitqah.

notes.official: Mitqah (ASV Mithkah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמִּתְקָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּחַשְׁמֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Mitqah and camped in Chashmonah.

notes.official: Chashmonah (ASV Hashmonah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵֽחַשְׁמֹנָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמֹסֵרֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Chashmonah and camped in Moserot.

notes.official: Moserot (ASV Moseroth); cf. Moserah, where Aharon dies according to Deut 10:6, against v 38 here (Mount Hor).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמֹּסֵר֑וֹת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בִּבְנֵ֥י יַעֲקָֽן׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Moserot and camped in Benei-Ya'aqan.

notes.official: Benei-Ya'aqan (ASV Bene-jaakan), 'the sons of Ya'aqan' (Gen 36:27; Deut 10:6 Be'erot Benei-Ya'aqan). The order Moserot, Benei-Ya'aqan, Chor-haGidgad, Yotvatah differs from Deut 10:6-7.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִבְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקָ֑ן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּחֹ֥ר הַגִּדְגָּֽד׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Benei-Ya'aqan and camped in Chor-haGidgad.

notes.official: Chor-haGidgad (ASV Hor-haggidgad; Deut 10:7 Gudgodah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵחֹ֣ר הַגִּדְגָּ֑ד וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּיָטְבָֽתָה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Chor-haGidgad and camped in Yotvatah.

notes.official: Yotvatah (ASV Jotbathah), 'a land of brooks of water' (Deut 10:7).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִיָּטְבָ֑תָה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעַבְרֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Yotvatah and camped in Avronah.

notes.official: Avronah (ASV Abronah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵֽעַבְרֹנָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֶצְי֥וֹן גָּֽבֶר׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Avronah and camped in Etzyon-Gever.

notes.official: Etzyon-Gever (ASV Ezion-geber), on the Gulf of Aqaba (1 Kgs 9:26; 22:49, where the Kings chapters use the same form).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵעֶצְי֣וֹן גָּ֑בֶר וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְמִדְבַּר־צִ֖ן הִ֥וא קָדֵֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Etzyon-Gever and camped in the wilderness of Tzin, that is, Qadesh.

notes.official: *bəmiḏbar-ṣin hiwʾ qāḏēš* 'in the wilderness of Tzin, that is, Qadesh' (ASV Zin, Kadesh): Qadesh(-Barnea), the base of chs. 13-20. Tzin is distinct from Sin (v 11). 'Qadesh' follows the qof rule of `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; genesis-woh prints both 'Qadesh' (16:14) and 'Kadesh' (14:7; 20:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקָּדֵ֑שׁ וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בְּהֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Qadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.

notes.official: Mount Hor, 'at the edge of the land of Edom' (20:22-23; central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעַל֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶל־הֹ֥ר הָהָ֛ר עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁ֑ם בִּשְׁנַ֣ת הָֽאַרְבָּעִ֗ים לְצֵ֤את בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֖י בְּאֶחָ֥ד לַחֹֽדֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: And Aharon the priest went up to Mount Hor by the mouth of YHWH and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Yisra'el had come out of the land of Mitsrayim, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.

notes.official: *ʿal-pî YHWH* 'by the mouth of YHWH'. The date of Aharon's death, the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year, is given only here (cf. 20:23-29; central `mitsrayim`; `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן בֶּן־שָׁלֹ֧שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמֹת֖וֹ בְּהֹ֥ר הָהָֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Aharon was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.

notes.official: A hundred and twenty-three years: Aharon was three years older than Moses (Ex 7:7; Deut 34:7).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲרָ֔ד וְהֽוּא־יֹשֵׁ֥ב בַּנֶּ֖גֶב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן בְּבֹ֖א בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official: A repetition of 21:1 at the point where the itinerary reaches Mount Hor; *bannegeḇ* 'in the Negev' (ASV 'in the South'), as there (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵהֹ֣ר הָהָ֑ר וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּצַלְמֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Mount Hor and camped in Tzalmonah.

notes.official: Tzalmonah (ASV Zalmonah).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִצַּלְמֹנָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּפוּנֹֽן׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Tzalmonah and camped in Punon.

notes.official: Punon (ASV), usually identified with Feinan, a copper-mining site in the Aravah. Some have connected the copper with the bronze serpent of 21:4-9 (Rothenberg 1972), but the text does not place that episode here.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִפּוּנֹ֑ן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאֹבֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Punon and camped in Ovot.

notes.official: Ovot (ASV Oboth), as 21:10-11.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֹבֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בְּעִיֵּ֥י הָעֲבָרִ֖ים בִּגְב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Ovot and camped in Iyye-ha'Avarim, on the border of Moab.

notes.official: *bəʿiyyê hāʿăḇārîm* Iyye-ha'Avarim (21:11), 'on the border of Moab'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵעִיִּ֑ים וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּדִיבֹ֥ן גָּֽד׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Iyyim and camped in Dibon-Gad.

notes.official: *mēʿiyyîm* 'from Iyyim' (ASV Iim), the short form of the name in v 44. Dibon-Gad (ASV Dibon-gad), Dibon (21:30) as rebuilt by Gad (32:34); modern Dhiban, where the Mesha stele was found.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִדִּיבֹ֣ן גָּ֑ד וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעַלְמֹ֥ן דִּבְלָתָֽיְמָה׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Dibon-Gad and camped in Almon-Divlatayim.

notes.official: Almon-Divlatayim (ASV Almon-diblathaim), probably Beit-Divlatayim (Jer 48:22; *bt dblten* on the Mesha stele, line 30).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵעַלְמֹ֣ן דִּבְלָתָ֑יְמָה וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בְּהָרֵ֥י הָעֲבָרִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י נְבֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Almon-Divlatayim and camped in the mountains of Avarim, before Nevo.

notes.official: *bəhārê hāʿăḇārîm* 'in the mountains of Avarim (ASV Abarim), before Nevo (ASV Nebo)', the range from which Moses views the land (27:12; Deut 32:49).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵהָרֵ֣י הָעֲבָרִ֑ים וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עַ֖ל יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from the mountains of Avarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Yarden at Yericho.

notes.official: *bəʿarḇōṯ môʾāḇ ʿal-yardēn yərēḥô* 'in the plains of Moab by the Yarden at Yericho' (ASV 'by the Jordan at Jericho'), the setting of Num 22-36 and of Deuteronomy; Yarden and Yericho as in the Kings chapters.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּחֲנ֤וּ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁמֹ֔ת עַ֖ד אָבֵ֣ל הַשִּׁטִּ֑ים בְּעַֽרְבֹ֖ת מוֹאָֽב׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And they camped by the Yarden, from Beit-haYeshimot as far as Avel-haShittim in the plains of Moab.

notes.official: Beit-haYeshimot (ASV Beth-jeshimoth) and Avel-haShittim (ASV Abel-shittim), 'meadow of the acacias' (cf. Shittim, 25:1; Josh 2:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֑ב עַל־יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵח֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Yarden at Yericho, saying,

notes.official: The closing section (vv 50-56) commands the conquest and leads into the boundaries and allotment of ch. 34.

paragraphs.text: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: "Speak to the children of Yisra'el and say to them, 'When you pass over the Yarden into the land of Canaan,

notes.official: *kî ʾattem ʿōḇərîm ʾeṯ-hayyardēn ʾel-ʾereṣ kənāʿan* 'When you pass over the Yarden into the land of Canaan' (central `eretz`). The message Moses is to deliver is set in single marks within YHWH's speech (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְה֨וֹרַשְׁתֶּ֜ם אֶת־כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וְאִ֨בַּדְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַשְׂכִּיֹּתָ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־צַלְמֵ֤י מַסֵּֽכֹתָם֙ תְּאַבֵּ֔דוּ וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־בָּמֹתָ֖ם תַּשְׁמִֽידוּ׃

i18n.en: then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured stones, and destroy all their molten images, and demolish all their high places;

notes.official:
*wəhôraštem ʾeṯ-kol-yōšəḇê hāʾāreṣ* 'then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land': *hôrîš* (Hiphil of *yrš*) with persons as object is 'dispossess, drive out'. *maśkîyyōṯām* 'their figured stones' (ASV, which brackets 'stones'; Lev 26:1 *ʾeḇen maśkîṯ*), *ṣalmê massēḵōṯām* 'their molten images', literally 'the images of their castings', and *bāmōṯām* 'their high places', the cultic platforms (new overlay `maskit-masekhah-bamah-cult-objects-numbers-33-52`). The verbs escalate from *ʾibbaḏtem* 'destroy' (twice) to *tašmîḏû* 'demolish'. The command parallels Ex 23:24; 34:13; Deut 7:5; 12:2-3 (central `eretz`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes vv 52-53 ('Ye shall destroy all their molten images ... and ye shall possess the land') and reads them as the chosen people destroying, on the creators' advice, the idols of the primitive tribes and occupying their territories. The line renders the cultic vocabulary by its lexical senses; the reading is recorded here only.

paragraphs.text: וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וִֽישַׁבְתֶּם־בָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י לָכֶ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֹתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: and you shall take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.

notes.official:
*wəhôraštem ʾeṯ-hāʾāreṣ wîšaḇtem-bāh* 'and you shall take possession of the land and dwell in it' (ASV): with 'the land' as object, *hôrîš* means 'take possession of', though some read 'dispossess (the inhabitants of) the land', as in v 52 (Levine 2000). The same root closes the verse, *lārešeṯ ʾōṯāh* 'to possess it' (central `eretz`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** This verse completes the canon's quotation of vv 52-53 ('... and ye shall possess the land'); see the note at v 52.

paragraphs.text: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם֩ אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ בְּגוֹרָ֜ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם לָרַ֞ב תַּרְבּ֤וּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתוֹ֙ וְלַמְעַט֙ תַּמְעִ֣יט אֶת־נַחֲלָת֔וֹ אֶל֩ אֲשֶׁר־יֵ֨צֵא ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛מָּה הַגּוֹרָ֖ל ל֣וֹ יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַטּ֥וֹת אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם תִּתְנֶחָֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: And you shall inherit the land by lot according to your families: to the larger you shall give the larger inheritance, and to the smaller you shall give the smaller inheritance; wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his; according to the tribes of your fathers you shall inherit.

notes.official: *wəhiṯnaḥaltem ʾeṯ-hāʾāreṣ bəḡôrāl* 'And you shall inherit the land by lot' (26:52-56): the size of each tribal allotment follows the size of the clan, its location the lot (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תוֹרִ֜ישׁוּ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָרֶץ֮ מִפְּנֵיכֶם֒ וְהָיָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תּוֹתִ֣ירוּ מֵהֶ֔ם לְשִׂכִּים֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וְלִצְנִינִ֖ם בְּצִדֵּיכֶ֑ם וְצָרֲר֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם עַל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יֹשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those whom you let remain of them shall be as pricks in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you dwell.

notes.official: *ləśikkîm bəʿênêḵem wəliṣnînim bəṣiddêḵem* 'as pricks in your eyes and as thorns in your sides' (ASV): *śēḵ* is a barb or splinter (only here). *wəṣārərû ʾeṯḵem* 'and they shall harass you'. The image recurs at Josh 23:13 and Judg 2:3 (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּמִּ֛יתִי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָהֶ֖ם אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass that as I thought to do to them, so I will do to you.'"

notes.official: *kaʾăšer dimmîṯî laʿăśôṯ lāhem ʾeʿĕśeh lāḵem* 'as I thought to do to them, so I will do to you': the warning of expulsion also given at Lev 18:24-28 and Deut 4:26-27.
